title: Momentum Index and Trigger Catalog
content:
Purpose:
This working doc defines a compact, pragmatic composite "momentum" index for customer health and a catalog of automated triggers mapped to next-best actions. Goal is a single-number momentum that is easy for CS to surface in QBRs and playbooks, while retaining signal-level explainability for escalations.

Audience:
- CSMs and CS managers preparing QBRs
- SuccessOps building dashboards and automated playbooks
- Data/Analytics for score validation and backtests

High-level design principles (working assumptions):
- Lightweight: single number + 4 supporting sub-scores (usage, depth, support, economics). CSMs should be able to explain the score in one sentence.
- Actionable: every bucket has a mapped trigger and playbook (can be automated or manual).
- Robust to noise: use short-term (14d) and medium-term (90d) windows to separate bursty behavior from trend.
- Calibrated: percentile-based normalization per cohort (ARR band + product plan) to avoid penalizing small customers unfairly.

Definitions and feature buckets (raw signals):
1) Usage Frequency (UF): daily active endpoints / expected DAU for customer size -> normalized.
   - Signals: API calls/day, chat sessions/day, embeddings requests/day.
   - Window: 14d moving average (MA14) and 90d MA90; use both.
2) Feature Depth (FD): percent of product modules used (e.g., streaming, tool-calls, reranking, caching).
   - Signals: distinct feature_count over 30d.
3) Quality Engagement (QE): user-visible error rate + average response latency anomalies + regressions flagged in tracking.
   - Signals: 5xx rate, >P95 latency deviations vs baseline, number of output quality complaints (tickets labeled "LLM-quality").
4) Support Intensity (SI): number and severity of support contacts; count of escalations; open P0/P1s.
   - Window: 30d open + SLA breaches in 90d.
5) Economics & Contract Signals (EC): spend velocity vs committed, trial-to-paid conversion, invoice disputes.
   - Signals: MRR run-rate vs committed, days past due.
6) Activation Momentum (AM): percent of new seats activated, time-to-first-successful-call for new users.

Normalization and weighting (draft):
- For each raw signal, compute z-score within cohort (ARR bucket x plan) then cap at +/-2.5 to limit outliers.
- Sub-scores:
  UF = weighted mean(z(API_calls), z(chat_sessions), z(embeddings)), weight 30% of momentum
  FD = z(feature_count), weight 25%
  QE = -z(quality_metric) (negative because higher errors reduce momentum), weight 20%
  SI = -z(support_intensity), weight 15%
  EC = z(economics_velocity), weight 10%
- Momentum Index (MI) = 50 + 10 * (0.3*UF + 0.25*FD + 0.2*QE + 0.15*SI + 0.1*EC) -> scale centered at 50 for interpretability (range roughly 20-80).
- Separate short-term momentum (MI14) using MA14 signals and medium-term MI90 using MA90; final Momentum = 0.6*MI14 + 0.4*MI90 to emphasize recency.

Risk bucket definitions (example thresholds - calibrate on historical churn):
- Healthy (MI >= 60). Low touch, auto NPS prompts + monthly check-in.
- Watch (50 <= MI < 60). Trigger: proactive outreach by CSM, health playbook A.
- At-risk (40 <= MI < 50). Trigger: immediate CSM review, create customer action plan, schedule technical deep-dive.
- Critical (MI < 40). Trigger: AE + CSM + Solutions eng war room; explore incentives + retention offer.

Trigger catalog (signal -> action):
- Sudden drop in MI14 > 12 points in 7d: immediate Slack alert to CSM, auto-schedule "Momentum Regression" triage (15 min), attach last 3 support tickets and recent errors.
- New P0 incident open: escalate to SRE/solutions with dedicated channel; CSM to send customer update within 4 hours.
- Feature drop-off: FD falls by 30% MoM for core module -> trigger "Adoption Re-engagement" playbook: in-product walkthrough, jumper sessions, usage templates.
- Spend vs committed drops > 25% in 30d: finance notifies CSM + AE; propose short-term promotional bundle if churn risk high.
- Trial cohort: if time-to-first-successful-call > 48h or activation < 25% in 7d -> auto onboarding nudge + CS-run onboarding session.

Playbook snippets (for CSMs):
- "Watch" playbook (score 50-59): 1) Review last 14d logs and QE metrics; 2) Send quick pulse email with 2 suggested actions; 3) Offer 30-min office hours.
- "At-risk" playbook (score 40-49): 1) Schedule technical deep-dive and exec sponsorship call; 2) Propose short-term optimization checklist (batching/kv cache/prompt tuning); 3) Set 14-day measurable objectives.
- "Critical" playbook (<40): 1) Convene cross-functional war room (CS + Eng + Sales); 2) Roll back recent config changes or fallback to compatible model variant; 3) Escalate billing hold review and legal if contract at risk.

Example SQL snippets (pseudo):
- cohort_norm: compute percentile per cohort:
  SELECT customer_id, PERCENT_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY cohort ORDER BY api_calls_90d) as p_api_calls FROM customer_usage_agg
- momentum calc (simplified):
  SELECT c.customer_id, 50 + 10 * (0.3*uf_z + 0.25*fd_z + 0.2*qe_z + 0.15*si_z + 0.1*ec_z) as momentum FROM computed_z c

Validation & calibration plan (TODOs):
- Backtest MI14/MI90 against 12-month churn labels in data warehouse (owner: DataOps).
- Tune weights using logistic regression to maximize AUC for 90-day churn prediction (owner: Analytics).
- Perform cohort-level calibration to align percentiles with expected action volumes (owner: SuccessOps).
- Run small pilot on 50 customers to validate playbook friction and false positives (owner: CS lead).

Dashboard and QBR usage guidance:
- CSM one-line for QBR: "Momentum 64 (steady +8 MoM): trending usage up, no support escalations; recommend upsell conversation in next 30d."
- Suggested visuals: sparkline MI14 vs MI90, stacked waterfall showing contribution of UF/FD/QE/SI/EC, recent trigger timeline.
- Exportable artifact: 1-pager scorecard with last 90d context + recommended next steps for execs.

Operational considerations (notes to implementers):
- Data freshness: MI14 must run daily; MI90 weekly. Ensure computed z-scores use last seen data and smoothing.
- Signal gaps: fallback to cohort median for missing signals. Track coverage metric and surface to CSM.
- Explainability: store top-3 contributing signals per customer for UI hover tooltip.
- Privacy/security: ensure customer-level logging for QE contains no PII; ticket text must be redacted.

Open questions / TODOs (rough):
- Should economics carry more weight for enterprise (maybe dynamic weighting by contract size)? (Action: run sensitivity test)
- How to incorporate qualitative inputs from CSMs (manual overrides) without polluting automated metric? Consider manual "flags" but keep separate audit trail.
- Do we want to include external signals (e.g., payment disputes flagged by Finance)? If yes, need integration scope.

Next steps (short):
1) Share doc with Analytics + SuccessOps for feasibility check (week 1).
2) Build prototype in Looker/Metabase using top 100 customers (week 2).
3) Run 90-day backtest and present results in CS Ops weekly (week 4).

Notes to self:
- Keep Momentum index easy for GTM to repeat in QBRs; avoid >6 buckets.
- Collect CSM feedback during pilot and iterate on thresholds not weights.
- Consider a separate "expansion momentum" variant focused on usage of premium features for upsell signals.

References and related artifacts:
- product adoption taxonomy (link in Confluence)
- CS playbook library: onboarding / re-engagement / renewal templates

End of draft.

(Comments welcome — this is intentionally compact; many edges left for analytics to fill in.)
